lines: d23: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Malik Melnyk is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d23: 🕯️ Malik Melnyk is dead — sickness. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d23: What Malik kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d23: "Malik's gone." Mateo looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Malik." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d23: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Frieda blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.

d23: 📖 LEARNED: Bodyguard (Level 1). In the wilds, when a blow is falling on someone beside you, you step into it. Once per fight, an attack meant for your ally lands on you instead. It hurts. That's the job.

d23: 📖 LEARNED: Diplomatic Incident (Level 1). Trust builds 2x faster. You're TOO good though — once per week you can start a diplomatic incident: villagers argue, you pick the winner (+trust with them, -trust with the loser).
d23: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d23: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Malik Melnyk, 23 days. The mantle passes to Frieda Qiu.
d23: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Frieda Qiu, 53 — a crossing guard. Their hands know different work now: Green Whisper.
d23: The village's quarrel was with Malik — and Malik is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d23: At the grave, Kwame, Ella, Mateo speak for Frieda — "Malik trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d23: The fire knew Frieda before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.

d42: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d42: 🕯️ Frieda is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.

d42: Emberhold watches to see if Haven holds without its dead. The bond is young — they're still deciding what Haven is, and grief delays the verdict.
